The bundled items are small, 2.70 MB in total. They are bundled in the package, so the zoo works offline and in CI. They are also mirrored to the Hugging Face Hub (PINNeAPPle-Labs/<name>, tag v<version>) by the "Publish zoo to the Hugging Face Hub" workflow. Larger items are Hub-only: same manifest, no bundled entry, lazy download.

docs.title: Models
docs.text: Candidate Where Verdict and reason Airfoil MeshGraphNet (fields + coefficients) Retrained on airfoil_rans_cst_re4e6_fields (scripts/zoo/train_airfoil_gnn.py: 60 epochs, hidden 48, 8 message-passing steps, seed 0, all fixed before training; 332 training runs of 85 shapes) Rejected by the zoo gate (2026-10-17). The coefficients pass every limit set before training: held-out shapes Cl MAE 0.0081, Cd MAPE 1.17 %; NACA reference Cl 0.0081, Cd 1.36 %; XFOIL NACA 2412 Cl 0.010, Cd 3.0 %; lift slope, monotonicity, symmetry and no-slip checks pass. The fields fail on the held-out shapes: relative L2 p 9.6 %, Ux 5.6 %, Uy 7.5 % (limit 5 %); nut 7.6 % (limit 15 %) passes. The predicted stagnation pressure reaches Cp 1.21, above Bernoulli's bound of 1.05. The checkpoint is not shipped, and the limits were not relaxed after seeing the test results. Next attempt, with a new configuration fixed before training: more message-passing steps or a wider network, and a pressure-weighted loss. The old apps/aero_optimizer checkpoint stays unshipped: its split cannot be reproduced on the published fields. Heat-sink natural-convection surrogate, unconstrained apps/heatsink_sizer/artifacts/surrogate_natural.pt Not shipped; replaced by heatsink_natural_mlp. Its own trust report's verdict is use_with_caution: the conductivity monotonicity has the right sign in only 94.9 % of held-out designs (strict). Under the zoo gate (≤ 1 % violations) that fails a physics check. The cause is that raising k by 5 % lowers the engine's resistance by only 0.13 % (median), below the fit error. The engine itself is monotone in k and in source width on all 400 designs probed. Black-hole accretion residual U-Net retrained on blackhole_riaf_density_256 (examples/black_hole_weather/README.md, "Zoo version") Not shipped: fails the mass-conservation check. The reference now has a resolution study, and its data ship as blackhole_riaf_density_256. The best variant (replicate padding, 3-block rollout loss, input noise, mass penalty) beats persistence with 95 % confidence at every lead from 60 to 2000 GM/c³ on the held-out trajectory: skill 0.27 [0.22, 0.31] at 2000 M, MAE 0.056 vs 0.076 for persistence and 0.073 for DMD. Its implied inflow agrees with the truth in sign at every start. But it breaks the training mass envelope in 37 % of frames, and 14–54 % with an extra mass-change penalty. It also loses to persistence at the first 20 GM/c³ frame. Out of distribution (α = 0.3) it beats persistence by 62 % at 2000 M [43, 76 %] and still breaks the envelope (21 %). The data are also not converged in the variability (see the dataset). ERA5 weather model, phase 1 examples/weather_forecasting/checkpoints/phase1_step15000_fp16.pt (40 MB) Not shipped. Its README calls it unfinished ("half way", rollout phases not run). z500 RMSE is 397 m at day 3, against 104–125 m for IFS / Pangu / NeuralGCM. Burgers PINN data/artifacts/examples/burgers_pinn/burgers_pinn.pt Not shipped. A toy model: rel. L2 is 0.060 against the exact solution with a max error of 0.22 (a 6 % error is not "good"), and it was saved from an mps device. Thermal-mass ODE twin (PINN, λ = 10) Benchmark repo, exp. 02 Not shipped. The PINN is no better than persistence (RMSE h6 2.972 °C vs 2.971). No weights are committed. Bumper-beam Transolver Benchmark repo, exp. 03 Not shipped. No weights. The classical POD+GP is better on the field (0.0055 vs 0.018). There is no mesh refinement study. The input deck is an Altair example under CC BY-NC 4.0, which is incompatible. Terramechanics "robust PINN" (2-D / 8-D) Benchmark repo, exp. 04 Not shipped. No weights. OOD rel. L2 is 0.37–0.68. Monotonicity fails for z up to 0.1 m. The in-range use case is covered by rover_contact_grc1_viper. Thermal channel ROM / FNO / DeepONet Benchmark repo, exp. 05 Not shipped. No weights. Pressure rel. L2 is about 0.99 (pressure fails); POD+DMDc diverged. The data now ships as thermal_channel_cfd; a temperature model is a candidate only if it passes the gate on the unseen families. Millennium probes (BSD, Hodge, Riemann, …) Benchmark repo, exp. 06 Not shipped. These are mathematical classifiers, not physics surrogates; the self-similar Burgers PINN failed (λ 0.418 vs 0.5). No weights. PDR velocity network (TLIO/DIVE) Benchmark repo, exp. 07 Not shipped. No weights. The data is RIDI (5.2 GB, not ours to redistribute), and it is out of the zoo's physics scope. Supersonic shock train Benchmark repo, exp. 08 Not shipped. There is no model, and the shock position is not grid-converged (x/H 6.98 / 4.55 / 3.30 on 3 grids). Equal-budget FNO / DeepONet / PINN (Burgers, Darcy, NS 2-D, airfoil, inverse heat) Benchmark repo, exp. 09 Not shipped yet. Only result tables are committed; checkpoints are gitignored. The FNO results are strong (Burgers 0.0033, NS 0.0084 rel. L2), and the generators are verified (Cole–Hopf 3e-13, Taylor–Green 1.7e-15), so these are the best v2 candidates. They will be retrained once pp.benchmark (branch feat/benchmark-api) is merged, because their data generators live there. Darcy is excluded: its OOD-shift check failed. All PINN rows failed (Darcy 0.87, airfoil Cd 99 %). runs/bench_PipeVanillaPINN.best.pt this repo Not shipped. A 1-epoch smoke-test artefact (val R² −0.23). pinneapple_worldmodel.ModelZoo, pinneapple_hub.from_pretrained this repo These are containers, not models: nothing was registered. The zoo reuses ModelCard, the trust report and ModelStore instead.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
Candidate Verdict and reason Airliner 3-D OpenFOAM results (apps/aero_optimizer/model/cfd3d/*.npz) Not shipped. It uses wall functions on a 0.4 M-cell half model with no mesh study. Lab: cylinder_lbm Shipped as cylinder_wake_lbm (Re 20–100). It ships after a resolution study (St within 0.7 % of D = 40), a saturation check and a corrected Strouhal estimate. Lab v1 read the raw FFT bin, 0.25 for every run. Runs at Re ≥ 140 need the Smagorinsky model, and Re 120 is 4.4 % off at D = 20; both are left out. Lab: car_lbm (and its car_surrogate) Rejected (2026-10-17). It is a 2-D lattice-Boltzmann LES (Smagorinsky Cs 0.1) at Re 500 with 64 cells per car length, about 15 % tunnel blockage and no resolution study. Its own notes say the bounce-back momentum exchange reads drag about 2× high, so drag comes from a control-volume balance instead. No grid-converged reference exists for the gate, and the surrogate inherits that. Lab: rom_study / cylinder_wake (data and DMD / OpInf models) Not shipped. The data is the same LBM cylinder at Re 100 as cylinder_wake_lbm (test split), which ships with its resolution study. The DMD (St 0.24438 vs FFT 0.24444) and Operator Inference models are fits to one trajectory, not reusable models. Lab: rom_study / beam_parametric (POD + RBF / GPR cantilever ROM) Candidate, not shipped. Its error on unseen designs is measured against FEM on the same mesh, and the FEM has no mesh study. It ships once a mesh study bounds the FEM error and a zoo adapter for ParametricPOD exists. Fin / plate inverse-convection fields Not shipped. These are outputs of a single case, not a dataset. pinneapple_data.datasets registry entries Not shipped as zoo items. They are generated on the fly. Several real_world entries silently fall back to synthetic placeholders. Zoo datasets are registered in that registry as zoo/<name>. ERA5 regional subset (rs_floods_2024_40.npy) Not shipped. It has no documented splits, and its companion model is unfinished. Shock-train fields (exp. 08) Not shipped: not grid-converged. Bumper-beam DoE (exp. 03) Excluded. It is 11 GB, not in git, and its input deck is CC BY-NC. Free-surface trough package Not shipped. It is 4 interFoam runs, not a dataset, and the 5 mm and 10 mm meshes settle into different flow states (not mesh-converged).

Everything excluded for client provenance has been left out of this document on purpose.

docs.title: How to add a model or dataset
docs.text:
1. Make it pass the gate above, with the evidence in the repository.
  2. Add it to pinneapple_hub/zoo/_catalog.py (card or dataset description, acceptance limits, guard metrics) and, for a model, an adapter in _models.py (predict, metrics, physics checks, fine-tuning hooks).
  3. Run python scripts/zoo/build_assets.py --rover DIR. This regenerates the assets, cards (with metrics and trust report) and the manifest; the build is deterministic. To add one item without touching the published ones, use --only NAME (with the training directory of a model trained by its own script, e.g. --heatsink-natural DIR) or --hub-only STAGING_DIR (Hub-only datasets).
  4. Run pytest tests/test_model_zoo.py.
  5. After the merge, the publish workflow uploads to the Hub.

docs.title: Return a 0–1 geometric similarity score with every surrogate prediction
docs.text:
Who has it: Simcenter/Altair PhysicsAI return a geometric similarity score; Ansys SimAI returns a confidence level telling whether a new design lies inside the training domain.

What PINNeAPPle already has: GeometryOODGuardrail, analysis/trust/trust_gate.py, conformal/ensemble UQ in pinneapple_analysis/uncertainty.

Proposal: Geometry embedding (geometry_features descriptors + curvature from geometry/ops/curvature.py) → distance to the training set (kNN/Mahalanobis) → calibrated to [0, 1] on a hold-out split. Return it with every prediction and in the evidence report.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Training designs score ≥ 0.9; a progressively deformed design gets a monotonically decreasing score; positive Spearman correlation between (1 − score) and the true error on a synthetic set.

Origin: docs/dev/ANALISE_FEATURES_COMERCIAIS.md §2 item 1

docs.title: Closed loop: the surrogate picks the next simulation (acquisition → campaign → retrain)
docs.text:
Who has it: HEEDS adaptive sampling, PhysicsX (UQ → new simulation), Neural Concept.

What PINNeAPPle already has: pinneapple_core/data.py::ActiveSampler, EI in design_optimizer, external_solvers/openfoam/campaign.py, pinneapple_registry.

Proposal: An orchestrator wiring acquisition function → campaign (OpenFOAM/LBM/any registry solver) → dataset store → retrain → next acquisition, stopping on validation error or budget.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): With a cheap solver (analytic function + stable_fluids), the active loop reaches the same error as an LHS of equal final size with ≤ 60% of the samples (mean over 5 seeds).

Origin: §2 item 2

docs.title: Pipeline 'CFD cases → field surrogate from STL / point cloud' + a real DoMINO
docs.text:
Who has it: Ansys SimAI (non-parametric), Simcenter PhysicsAI, Luminary SHIFT (DoMINO/GeoTransolver), Emmi AB-UPT.

What PINNeAPPle already has: Transolver, MeshGraphNet, physicsnemo_bridge, lpm.py. Note: pinneapple_physics/pinn_solver/domino.py is a domain-decomposition PINN, not NVIDIA's DoMINO — the name is misleading.

Proposal: Ready-made pipeline: folder of OpenFOAM cases → dataset (surface + volume) → training (Transolver / DoMINO via the bridge) → fields + Cd/Cl → report. Rename or clearly document the current domino.py.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Reproducible AhmedML benchmark (CC-BY-SA) reporting the Cd error and comparing it with a published number.

Origin: §2 item 3

docs.title: Export ROMs and surrogates as FMUs (co-simulation)
docs.text:
Who has it: Ansys Twin Builder, Simcenter ROM Builder (FMI + ONNX), Altair/Siemens romAI.

What PINNeAPPle already has: ROMs (POD, DMD, OpInf, neural ROM), ONNX/TorchScript export; modelica/fmi_runner.py only imports FMUs; the new fmu_inspect.py validates them.

Proposal: Package linear ROMs (POD/DMD/OpInf) as FMI 2.0/3.0 co-simulation FMUs from generated C (no runtime dependency), and neural ROMs through ONNX Runtime.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): The generated FMU passes inspect_fmu (exports every required function), simulates with fmpy and reproduces the Python ROM to 1e-10.

Origin: §2 item 4

docs.title: PINNeAPPle MCP server generated from PhysicsToolRegistry
docs.text:
Who has it: PyAnsys (MCP servers for PyFluent/PyMechanical/PyMAPDL), Luminary SDK (documented MCP server).

What PINNeAPPle already has: PhysicsToolRegistry already carries input_schema/output_schema; agent_loop uses the registry.

Proposal: Generate MCP tools from the registry (stdio), with an allowlist and PhysicsGuardrail on outputs.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): tools/list exposes the registered tools; a reference_license_policy call and one solver call return valid JSON.

Origin: §2 item 5

docs.title: SIMP topology optimization (2-D compliance) on top of solid_fem
docs.text:
Who has it: Ansys Mechanical/Discovery, STAR-CCM+ adjoint topology optimization, SU2, OpenFOAM adjointOptimisation.

What PINNeAPPle already has: Absent.

Proposal: SIMP with density filter and OC/MMA updates, 2-D compliance, on solid_fem.py.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Reproduce Sigmund's MBB beam ('99-line code', 2001): final compliance within 1% of the published value on the same mesh.

Origin: §2 item 6

docs.title: Solution-adaptive mesh refinement (quadtree, wavelet/gradient criterion)
docs.text:
Who has it: CONVERGE (AMR every step), Basilisk (adapt_wavelet), Luminary SDK.

What PINNeAPPle already has: Static refinement only (boundary layers, curvature, snappy levels).

Proposal: 2-D quadtree with a wavelet criterion for fvm and shallow_water_fv.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Ritter dam break: same L1 error as the fine uniform grid with ≤ 40% of the cells.

Origin: §2 item 7

docs.title: Multi-fidelity surrogate (Kennedy–O'Hagan co-kriging)
docs.text:
Who has it: optiSLang AI+, HEEDS data reuse, COMSOL.

What PINNeAPPle already has: Transfer/meta-learning exist; explicit multi-fidelity does not.

Proposal: Autoregressive co-kriging on the NumPy GP in design_optimizer (e.g. coarse LBM + fine OpenFOAM).

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Forrester functions (closed form): co-kriging with 4 HF + 11 LF points beats an HF-only GP in RMSE.

Origin: §2 item 8

docs.title: Hybrid dynamic ROM (physics + learned residual) calibrated online from sensors
docs.text:
Who has it: Twin Builder (Neural ODE, TFT, Hammerstein LPV, fusion modeling), ROM Builder (LSTM/GRU).

What PINNeAPPle already has: Neural ROM, Koopman, SINDy, Kalman, 4D-Var — but not the physics + residual composition updated online.

Proposal: Physics ROM + learned correction, updated by Kalman/EnKF inside digital_twin.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Synthetic system with a known missing term: the learned residual converges to it (error < 5%).

Origin: §2 item 9

docs.title: Polynomial chaos expansion + Sobol indices for UQ and sensitivity
docs.text:
Who has it: optiSLang, COMSOL Uncertainty Quantification Module.

What PINNeAPPle already has: Conformal / ensemble / MC-dropout; no PCE.

Proposal: Regression PCE (Hermite/Legendre) with Sobol indices computed analytically from the coefficients.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Ishigami function: first-order and total Sobol indices within 1% of the closed-form values.

Origin: §2 item 10

docs.title: Geometry encoders (PointNet / DGCNN; B-rep UV-Net later)
docs.text:
Who has it: Neural Concept, Simcenter PhysicsAI (geometric deep learning).

What PINNeAPPle already has: geometry_features, geometry_intelligence (hand-crafted descriptors).

Proposal: PointNet/DGCNN encoders in pinneapple_neural/architectures, used by the similarity score and the raw-geometry surrogate.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Permutation invariance tested; accuracy reported on a ModelNet10 subset.

Origin: §2 item 11

docs.title: LBM D3Q27 cumulant collision + STL voxelization + FP16 storage
docs.text:
Who has it: ultraFluidX, PowerFLOW, XFlow, M-Star, SimScale Pacefish, FluidX3D (FP16 storage).

What PINNeAPPle already has: lbm.py: D2Q9/D3Q19 BGK + Smagorinsky; lbm_tunnel.

Proposal: D3Q27 cumulant collision, STL voxelization (GPU via torch), FP16 storage with FP32 arithmetic (the idea only — FluidX3D is non-commercial, no code reuse).

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): 3-D Poiseuille and Taylor–Green against exact solutions; sphere at Re = 100 with Cd within 3% of the Schiller–Naumann correlation.

Origin: §3

docs.title: Incremental FNO (iFNO): grow Fourier modes during training
docs.text:
Who has it: neuraloperator IncrementalFNOTrainer (MIT); George et al., TMLR 2024.

What PINNeAPPle already has: FNO in architectures/neural_operators/fno.py with fixed modes.

Proposal: Training callback (loss-gap and explained-variance rules) that increases the FNO modes.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): 1-D Burgers: same final accuracy as fixed-mode FNO with fewer training FLOPs (fixed seed).

Origin: ledger: neuraloperator

docs.title: MultiAdam optimizer for multi-term PINN losses
docs.text:
Who has it: PINNacle src/optimizer/multiadam.py (MIT).

What PINNeAPPle already has: NTK weighting and Adam → L-BFGS exist; MultiAdam does not.

Proposal: Separate Adam moment statistics per loss group.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Poisson with badly balanced boundary terms: lower relative error than plain Adam over 3 seeds.

Origin: ledger: PINNacle

docs.title: MAPDL .rst result reader and a PyFluent driver
docs.text:
Who has it: PyAnsys pymapdl-reader and pyfluent (MIT).

What PINNeAPPle already has: Readers for Abaqus, Exodus, CGNS, Fluent mesh, STAR-CCM+; Fluent driven by journal files.

Proposal: .rst reader (optional pymapdl-reader dependency) into UPD; a PyFluent path in external_solvers/ansys.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): pymapdl-reader's own example .rst file read with displacements equal to the reference library's.

Origin: ledger: PyAnsys

docs.title: In-browser PDE preview (SymbolicPDE → GLSL), VisualPDE-style
docs.text:
Who has it: VisualPDE (MIT) — located with REA: setRDEquations, url_codec, auto steps-per-frame.

What PINNeAPPle already has: pinneapple_app/frontend (React/Vite); SymbolicPDE.

Proposal: Emit GLSL from a 2-D reaction–diffusion ProblemSpec, run it in the frontend, keep the state shareable in the URL.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Gray–Scott: steady pattern matches the NumPy solver (correlation > 0.99) on 5 presets.

Origin: ledger: VisualPDE

docs.title: PhysicsNeMo models not yet exposed: FIGConvNet, TopoDiff, DLWP-HEALPix
docs.text:
Who has it: NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo (Apache-2.0).

What PINNeAPPle already has: physicsnemo_bridge exists; these models are not exposed.

Proposal: Expose through the bridge first (no reimplementation); reimplement only where justified.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Forward smoke test + one small training case per model.

Origin: ledger: PhysicsNeMo

docs.title: REA: native binary analysis (FMUs, solvers) with a Ghidra provider
docs.text:
Who has it: REA open_binary + Ghidra/Hopper/IDA providers.

What PINNeAPPle already has: rea_bridge covers JavaScript and provenance; fmu_inspect covers the ELF symbol table. Ghidra could not be installed in the sandbox (GitHub Releases download blocked).

Proposal: rea setup with Ghidra on a machine with access; ReaClient.open_binary/decompile wrappers + a native-Evidence summarizer.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Decompile fmi2DoStep from a Reference-FMU and locate the call into the integrator, with Evidence.

Origin: docs/dev/REA_INTEGRATION.md

docs.title: Adjoint: MMA optimizer and volumetric B-spline parameterization
docs.text:
Who has it: OpenFOAM ESI adjointOptimisation, SU2 (RBF, Hicks–Henne).

What PINNeAPPle already has: ContinuousAdjointSolver, ShapeParametrization.

Proposal: MMA (Svanberg 1987) and volumetric B-spline morphing boxes.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): MMA reproduces the optimum of Svanberg's test problem; zero control-point displacement leaves the geometry unchanged.

Origin: §3

docs.title: Design study as a first-class object (Study → Designs → Scenarios + comparison view)
docs.text:
Who has it: Autodesk CFD Design Study Automation, COMSOL Model Manager, Simcenter Studio.

What PINNeAPPle already has: pinneapple_lab, pinneapple_registry.

Proposal: Study/Design/Scenario hierarchy in the registry + a comparison view in pinneapple_app.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Round trip: a saved and reloaded study returns identical results; the comparison sorts by KPI.

Origin: §2 item 12

docs.title: Parametric RBF morphing of tessellated geometry (no CAD needed)
docs.text:
Who has it: STAR-CCM+ 2506 Parametric Morphing, SU2 RBF deformation.

What PINNeAPPle already has: Absent (optimization needs parametric geometry).

Proposal: RBF morphing with control points and parameter vectors acting on an STL.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Exact interpolation at control points; zero displacement outside the support; no inverted elements (positive Jacobian).

Origin: §2 item 13

docs.title: Viewer with hash-keyed inference cache and surrogate-vs-truth diff
docs.text:
Who has it: NVIDIA Omniverse digital-twins-for-fluid-simulation blueprint (SHA256-keyed .npz cache).

What PINNeAPPle already has: twin3d viewer, pinneapple_app.

Proposal: Re-infer on every parameter change, cache by input hash, diff tab against ground truth.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Same input → same hash and a cache hit; zero diff when surrogate equals truth.

Origin: §2 item 15

docs.title: The Well adapter: WellDataset → PINNeAPPle dense volumes + leaderboard-comparable metrics
docs.text:
Who has it: PolymathicAI The Well (BSD-2-Clause): 16 physics datasets (fluids, MHD, supernovae, acoustics, biology), WellDataset loader, VRMSE / binned spectral MSE / Wasserstein-1 / windowed DTW metrics.

What PINNeAPPle already has: Planned in ROADMAP §4 (pinneapple_data.adapters.well_adapter), not implemented. field_metrics now reports vrmse and pearson with The Well's definitions.

Proposal: Adapter to the load_dense_volumes format; streaming from the HF Hub; binned spectral MSE with The Well's default log-spaced bins; register the datasets in pinneapple_catalog.resources with their license.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Round trip on the MHD_64 (or smallest) split: shapes/channels/time match the HDF5 metadata; VRMSE of the persistence baseline (u(t+1) = u(t)) reproduced within 5% of the value in The Well paper.

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: The Well

docs.title: Procedural PDE datasets on the fly (APEBench-style) using the new ETDRK4
docs.text:
Who has it: APEBench (MIT): datasets are generated procedurally by a spectral ETDRK reference solver (Exponax) instead of downloaded; scenarios are parameterized by normalized 'difficulty' coefficients; autoregressive rollout metrics.

What PINNeAPPle already has: numerical_solvers/etdrk4.py (S27), PDE presets, field_metrics.

Proposal: pinneapple_data.procedural: periodic 1/2/3-D scenarios (advection, diffusion, Burgers, KdV, KS, Gray–Scott, Swift–Hohenberg) with seeded random ICs, generated on demand; difficulty parameterization γ_j = α_j N^j 2^(j-1) D with α_j = a_j Δt / L^j (Exponax extract_normalized_coefficients_from_difficulty); rollout nRMSE/VRMSE curves.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Deterministic: same seed → identical dataset; linear scenarios match the exact Fourier solution to 1e-10; cross-check against Exponax trajectories when available.

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: APEBench / Exponax

docs.title: Neural-corrected coarse solver trained through the rollout (solver-in-the-loop)
docs.text:
Who has it: APEBench CorrectedStepper; PhiFlow 'solver-in-the-loop' (Um et al., NeurIPS 2020).

What PINNeAPPle already has: Differentiable torch solvers (fvm, lbm, spectral), hybrid surrogates (hybrid_surrogate_physics).

Proposal: Wrap a coarse differentiable solver with a learned correction (sequential or parallel composition) trained by unrolling k steps.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): 1-D Burgers at 4× coarsening: corrected stepper error < 50% of the uncorrected coarse solver over a 100-step rollout (3 seeds).

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: APEBench / PhiFlow

docs.title: Differentiable implicit linear solves with matrix construction by tracing (PhiFlow-style)
docs.text:
Who has it: PhiFlow (MIT): sparse matrices built automatically by tracing a linear function; preconditioned solvers with implicit (adjoint) gradients; dimension-agnostic code.

What PINNeAPPle already has: Implicit steps in fdm.py/fvm.py assemble matrices by hand; gradients through solves are not implicit.

Proposal: A linear_solve(f, rhs) helper: trace f to a sparse matrix once, solve with CG/BiCGStab, backward pass by solving the transposed system (implicit differentiation), no unrolled iterations.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Gradient of a Poisson-solve objective matches finite differences to 1e-6 and costs one extra solve; traced matrix equals the hand-assembled 5-point Laplacian exactly.

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: PhiFlow

docs.title: Nektar++ bridge (spectral/hp element, MIT) for high-order reference data
docs.text:
Who has it: Nektar++ 5.9 (MIT): CG/DG/HDG/flux-reconstruction spectral/hp, incompressible and compressible N–S, linear stability and adjoint, curvilinear high-order meshes.

What PINNeAPPle already has: Bridges to OpenFOAM, FEniCS, CalculiX, FluidX3D, MuJoCo…; no high-order solver.

Proposal: Session-XML generation from a ProblemSpec, runner (subprocess/Docker), field reader into UPD — same pattern as the OpenFOAM bridge.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Kovasznay flow: L2 error converges spectrally with polynomial order (≥ 1 decade per +2 orders) against the exact solution.

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: Nektar++ (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nektar%2B%2B)

docs.title: JAX-Fluids as an optional external solver (GPL: subprocess bridge, no code reuse)
docs.text:
Who has it: JAX-Fluids 2.0 (GPL-3.0): fully differentiable compressible two-phase solver (level-set / diffuse interface), level-set immersed boundaries, multi-GPU.

What PINNeAPPle already has: jax_cfd_solver.py (incompressible, Apache); no compressible two-phase solver.

Proposal: Out-of-process bridge (case JSON in, HDF5 out) behind an optional extra, never imported in-process or vendored; clean-room policy for any method taken from it (ledger).

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Sod shock tube run through the bridge matches the exact Riemann solution (L1 density error decreasing with resolution).

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: JAX-Fluids

docs.title: ParaView Catalyst 2 in-situ adaptor for solvers and surrogates
docs.text:
Who has it: ParaView 6.2 (BSD-3-Clause, Copyright.txt): Catalyst 2 with Conduit Blueprint; NekRS/FluidX3D/M-Star render while running.

What PINNeAPPle already has: PyVista/VTK export, trame, Rerun bridge; nothing streams fields in situ from the native solvers.

Proposal: Optional catalyst adaptor publishing mesh + fields as Conduit Blueprint every N steps from fvm, lbm, stable_fluids and surrogate rollouts.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Blueprint verification (conduit.blueprint.verify) passes for each published step; field values round-trip exactly.

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: ParaView

docs.title: Neural networks inside variational forms (firedrake.ml-style) in the FEniCS bridge
docs.text:
Who has it: Firedrake (LGPL-3.0, clean-room): fem_operator / ml_operator embed PyTorch/JAX models in UFL forms with adjoints.

What PINNeAPPle already has: fenics_bridge, hybrid surrogates; no NN term inside a weak form.

Proposal: External-operator term in a FEniCS form evaluated by a torch model, with the adjoint provided by torch autograd (method from the published paper, not Firedrake code).

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Poisson with a learned source equal to the exact source: FE solution matches the manufactured solution at the FE discretisation error; gradient check against finite differences.

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: Firedrake

docs.title: NVIDIA Warp backend: warp.fem weak forms + zero-copy torch interop
docs.text:
Who has it: NVIDIA Warp 1.18 (Apache-2.0): @wp.kernel with wp.Tape autodiff, warp.fem integrands on grid/tet/hex geometries, wp.to_torch via DLPack.

What PINNeAPPle already has: Warp only indirectly through the Newton bridge; ROADMAP §3 lists Warp as a candidate differentiable backend.

Proposal: compute_backends.warp: zero-copy tensors, a Poisson/elasticity example in warp.fem, differentiable particle step for particle_dynamics.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): warp.fem Poisson matches the manufactured solution with O(h^2) convergence; Warp vs torch gradients agree to 1e-6.

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: NVIDIA Warp

docs.title: RBF / Kriging / EBF approximation models with training-set outlier detection
docs.text:
Who has it: Dassault Isight approximation models (RSM, Kriging, RBF, EBF), COMSOL surrogate training (GP, PCE, DNN), 3DEXPERIENCE outlier exploration.

What PINNeAPPle already has: NumPy GP in design_optimizer; no RBF surrogate; no outlier screening of training data.

Proposal: RBF interpolant (thin-plate/multiquadric with polynomial tail), ordinary Kriging, leave-one-out error, and an outlier score per training sample.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): RBF reproduces polynomials of the tail degree exactly; LOO error of Kriging on the Branin function within published ranges; an injected corrupted sample is ranked first by the outlier score.

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: SIMULIA / COMSOL

docs.title: Onshape connector: sample configuration parameters and export geometry for DOE
docs.text:
Who has it: Onshape REST API (configurations, encodeConfigurationMap, STL/STEP/Parasolid export); Luminary × Onshape partner app generating SHIFT-Wing variants.

What PINNeAPPle already has: STEP via gmsh, CadQuery; Onshape appears only in the resource catalog.

Proposal: pinneapple_design.geometry.io.onshape: read configuration parameters, LHS over them, export STL per variant, record document/version IDs as dataset lineage.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Mocked API round-trip test; on a public demo document, two different configurations produce meshes with different volumes matching Onshape's mass properties.

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: Onshape

docs.title: Rescale REST connector: run a DOE campaign on Rescale and pull results
docs.text:
Who has it: Rescale API v2 (jobs, submit, statuses, files), AI Physics dataset format (PyVista-compatible).

What PINNeAPPle already has: SLURM script generation, Prefect flows, file-lock sharded OpenFOAM campaigns; no managed cloud backend.

Proposal: A campaign backend that submits each DOE point as a Rescale job, polls, downloads outputs and registers them in pinneapple_registry.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Contract tests against recorded API responses; resumable after interruption (no duplicate submissions).

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: Rescale

docs.title: COMSOL bridge through MPh (parameter sweeps → dataset)
docs.text:
Who has it: COMSOL 6.3/6.4 surrogate training, Model Manager; MPh (MIT, community) drives COMSOL's Java API from Python.

What PINNeAPPle already has: Nothing beyond mentions in the tool-recommendation tables.

Proposal: Optional bridge: open .mph, set parameters, solve, export scalars and fields to UPD/xarray; reuse the DOE samplers.

Acceptance (rule D1 — independent reference): Skipped without a COMSOL licence; with one, a parametric sweep of a shipped tutorial model reproduces COMSOL's own table to 1e-9.

Origin: mapping 2026-10-12: COMSOL

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Integrates REA (Reverse Engineer Anything, MIT) as the third source of the research pipeline, with a license gate and a provenance ledger, and adds components extracted from 50+ reference projects. Every new component is tested against an independent reference — closed form, exact solution, identity or an independent implementation (rule D1).

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
• pinneapple_tools/rea_bridge/
  • CLI client: PINNEAPPLE_REA_BIN > rea > npx rea-agents@6.4.0.
  • JS Evidence → feature map (functions, call graph, exact lines), plus locate(keywords).
  • ELF layout → exported symbols.
  • License gate (adapt / clean_room / reference_only).
  • HarvestLedger, which refuses adapted code from copyleft projects.
  • PhysicsToolRegistry.register_all() → reference_license_policy, rea_analyze_javascript, rea_locate_feature.
  • .mcp.json: REA MCP server for coding agents.
  • docs/dev/REA_INTEGRATION.md, docs/dev/ANALISE_FEATURES_COMERCIAIS.md (feature-gap analysis vs Ansys, Siemens, Luminary, PhysicsX, Neural Concept, Godela, Omniverse and 20+ CFD codes).
  • docs/dev/rea_harvest/ledger.json (53 projects).
  • docs/dev/issues/ (35 issue drafts) + scripts/publish_issues.sh.

docs.title: New components
docs.text: File Origin (license, method) Validation numerical_solvers/etdrk4.py (S27) Cox–Matthews / Kassam–Trefethen (clean-room vs Dedalus GPL); blow-up guard from VisualPDE via REA exact exp(Lt), measured 4th order, linear KdV, Burgers vs Cole–Hopf (< 1e-9), matches Exponax to 4.5e-14 on chaotic KS numerical_solvers/stable_fluids.py (S28) WebGL-Fluid-Simulation via REA (MIT) div = 0 to round-off, Taylor–Green 1st order, exact translation analysis/validation/field_metrics.py PDEBench (MIT, fRMSE fixed), The Well (BSD-2: VRMSE, Pearson) Parseval 1D/2D/3D, single-mode bands, closed-form VRMSE analysis/uncertainty/posterior_metrics.py (CRPS) Gneiting et al.; Earth-2 Studio usage integral definition, pairwise identity, deterministic limit design/geometry/ops/curvature.py PhysicsNeMo (Apache, independent NumPy) exact Gauss–Bonnet, sphere/cylinder/plane external_solvers/modelica/fmu_inspect.py FMI headers (BSD-2), REA on Modelica Reference-FMUs parser = nm -D = REA/pwntools on 15 FMUs pinneapple_twin3d UsdPhysics export OpenUSD schemas OpenUSD's own physics parser recognises scene, bodies, colliders, material

docs.title: Fixes relative to the references
docs.text:
• WebGL-Fluid: a 5-point Jacobi solve with central div/grad is inconsistent, so the divergence never reaches zero. Replaced by a consistent spectral projection.
  • PDEBench: the 2-D/3-D fRMSE drops negative frequencies. Now the full spectrum is binned.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
62 new tests pass (several also end to end with the real REA, Exponax and usd-core). Integration tests skip cleanly when REA, Exponax, usd-core or the built Reference-FMUs are absent. The full suite was not run (no torch in the sandbox), so run pytest before merging. In method_status.json only S27/S28 were inserted: a full regeneration would drop the PINNeAPPle-CFD references, which aren't available there.

🤖 Generated with Claude Code

https://claude.ai/code/session_01TTWeeDL5NNNcvZGQPVBuW6

docs.title: Examples as flows
docs.text:
Every examples/* folder, the flow that reproduces it in Flow Studio (Open... -> Examples) and the outcome of running that flow. docs.title: First PINN
docs.text:
A minimal experiment connects:

  • ProblemDefinition
  • Domain/Geometry sampling
  • Model
  • Physics objective (residuals + constraints)
  • Solver (training policy)
  • Backend (execution)

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer.
  • Nothing else to get started: numpy, scipy, torch, sympy and matplotlib come with the package.

docs.title: From PyPI
docs.text:
pip install pinneapple

Then check the machine, not just the import:

pinneapple doctor start

That prints one line per thing it checked and, for each missing item, the command that fixes it.

docs.title: Profiles: install for the work you intend to do
docs.text:
Instead of picking among the small extras, install the bundle that matches your work:

profile pip install ... for start pinneapple the first week: solve a preset, plot a field, train one small network cfd pinneapple[cfd] geometry, meshing, 3-D viewing; OpenFOAM and CalculiX are separate installs research pinneapple[pinn,uq,viz3d,jax_cfd] PINNs, uncertainty, JAX, publication figures enterprise pinneapple[enterprise] serving, signatures, the CI linter, the hub, the MCP server everything pinneapple[all] every extra the package declares

pinneapple doctor <profile> checks exactly the set above, and pinneapple doctor all lists every extra with the ones missing here.

Two things the Python package cannot install for you, and doctor cfd reports:

  • OpenFOAM for the CFD campaigns: install it (or the ESI build) and source its environment, so blockMesh and simpleFoam are on PATH.
  • FEniCS for the 18 presets whose reference solver is fenics: pip install "pinneapple[fenics]". Without it those presets train a network instead, and pp.card(name) says so.

docs.title: From a checkout, for development
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/barrosyan/PINNeAPPle.git
cd PINNeAPPle
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # Linux/Mac
# .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1  # Windows PowerShell
pip install -U pip
pip install -e ".[dev]"

Verify the checkout:

python -c "import pinneapple as pp; pp.info()"
pytest tests/test_public_api.py tests/test_onboarding.py -q

docs.title: Colab
docs.text: The notebooks in notebooks/colab/ install the package in their first cell; open one from the badge in the README.

docs.title: Project Layout
docs.text: PINNeAPPle's pinneapple_* packages map to framework layers — see Architecture → Package Layers. This page is the map of everything around those packages: the top-level directories that hold the web app, runnable code samples, operational scripts, and example projects.

docs.title: pinneapple_app/
docs.text: The FastAPI + frontend web application for benchmarking PINN models through a browser instead of a script. backend/ is a FastAPI service (main.py, routers/, core/); frontend/ is a Vite/React app (src/, index.html, tailwind.config.js). Dockerfile.backend, Dockerfile.frontend, docker-compose.yml, and nginx.conf compose the two into a deployable service. This is the only directory in the repo meant to run as a long-lived server rather than a one-off script.

docs.title: examples/
docs.text: Runnable scripts organized by package/topic (architectures/, data_pipeline/, geometry/, numerical_solvers/, pde_environment/, pinn_solver/, problem_designer/, trainer/, time_series/, benchmark_suite/, hpo_experiments/, arena_pipelines/, systems/, worldmodel/, use_cases/, visualizations/, end_to_end/, plus comparison folders like vs_physicsnemo/ and pinneapple_and_physicsnemo/), meant to be run from the repo root, e.g. python examples/data_pipeline/01_physical_sample_basics.py (see examples/README.md). Also holds a few standalone results-generation scripts (generate_chassis_results.py, embed_results.py, export_pdf.py) and their output folders (_out/, _runs*/).

docs.title: templates/
docs.text: A curated, numbered set of ~35 standalone scripts (01_basic_pinn.py through 35_jax_backend.py), each demonstrating one capability end-to-end in a single file: domain decomposition, causal training, CSG geometry, shape optimization, CAD-to-CFD, meta-learning, world models, rigid-body/MPM simulation, uncertainty quantification, transfer learning, inverse problems, neural operators (FNO/DeepONet), active learning, model serving/export, digital twins, GNN mesh models, ROMs, time-series models, Arena benchmarking, Koopman autoencoders, Zarr data pipelines, LLM-assisted problem design, physics validation, RANS turbulence, 3D heat conduction, and the JAX backend. Where examples/ is organized by package and includes multi-step pipelines, templates/ is organized by feature — one file, one concept, meant to be read top-to-bottom as a reference.

docs.title: scripts/
docs.text: Operational runbook scripts for a specific end-to-end MVP flow (a 2D flow- past-obstacle case), documented in scripts/README.md: cosmos/ (optional scene-to-spec generation via a Cosmos endpoint), omniverse/ (USD generation and point sampling, run inside Omniverse Kit), mvp/ (bundle validation and local Arena matrix runs), arena/ (benchmark run + leaderboard), and dev/ for miscellaneous development helpers, plus two top-level utilities: update_imports.py and validate_model_card.py. This is a runbook for one concrete pipeline, not a general-purpose scripts folder.

docs.title: tools/
docs.text: Repository build tooling. Currently just gen_api_docs.py — the mkdocs-gen-files script that generates docs/api/ and docs/SUMMARY.md's API navigation section from the pinneapple_* packages' docstrings at mkdocs build time (see API Reference and Package Layers).

docs.title: projects/
docs.text: A worked example of a full physics project built on top of the framework, rather than a framework component itself: main.py runs an 8-step pipeline (geometry generation → point sampling from an STL → scenario spec generation → OpenFOAM sampling across scenarios → bundle export → PINN training → operator-model training → evaluation/ranking) for the heat_channel_obstacle_3d/ case, driven by configs/ and scripts/pipeline/. Use this directory as a template for structuring a new project, not as library code to import from.

docs.title: notebooks/
docs.text: Jupyter notebooks for interactive walkthroughs, e.g. PINNeAPPle_Demo_Heat3D_Laplace.ipynb — useful for exploring a result interactively after a script-based run, less suited to automated pipelines.

docs.title: benchmarks/
docs.text: Micro-benchmarks of the library's own performance and internals — not physics benchmarks. data_io_bench.py and shard_balance_bench.py measure pinneapple_data I/O and sharding performance; _latency.py measures call overhead. _out/ holds checked-in results (CSV/JSON/plots) from a prior run. Contrast with pinneapple_tools.benchmark_suite (see Researcher & Benchmarking), which benchmarks models, not the library itself.

docs.title: pp.new: a project of your own, outside this repository
docs.text:
templates/ and examples/ belong to the library. A user's own work goes in its own folder, which pp.new (or pinneapple new) writes:

pinneapple new my_study --template plain --preset poisson_2d
cd my_study && python run.py
template what the user writes what the folder holds plain case.yaml only run.py, case.yaml, README.md, requirements.txt, results/ research case.yaml, then study.py as the study grows the above plus study.py, notebook.ipynb, experiment.json cfd case.yaml (preset, parameter, values) sweep.py, case.yaml, README.md, results/cases.csv, results/qoi.png

Every generated path is relative to the folder, so the project runs from any working directory and can be copied or versioned on its own. When the chosen preset cannot run on that machine, the folder also gets fallback.py: the same physics on a box the user defines, and the runner's error message points at it.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Problem → Data/Geometry → Model → PINN/Physics → Solver → Backend → Metrics

Use this order to structure experiments and keep components swappable.

docs.title: Start here (docs)
docs.text: The page you are reading is the site version of START_HERE.md at the repository root. Same content, same four commands; that file is the one that gets executed by tests/test_front_door.py, so it is the one to trust if the two ever disagree.

docs.title: Four commands, before any physics
docs.text:
pip install pinneapple
pinneapple doctor start          # is this machine ready? one fix command per missing item
pinneapple recommend "problem"    # which preset, which method, which model, and why
pinneapple card <preset>          # what it takes, what it gives back, the program to run
pinneapple new my_study           # a project of your own: case.yaml + runner + README

In Python: pp.doctor(profile), pp.recommend(text), pp.card(name), pp.new(name, ...).

docs.title: Which path is yours
docs.text: you are start with then an engineer with a problem, and no Python pinneapple new my_case --template plain; edit case.yaml only installation, project layout learning physics-AI pp.card("burgers_1d"), then pp.solve with the closed form, then train and compare first PINN, choosing a method a researcher with pipelines and papers pinneapple new my_study --template research adding an experiment, IPython a team putting this behind a product pinneapple doctor enterprise physics checks in CI, pp_validate

docs.title: Describing your own PDE: one route, documented
docs.text:
Two code paths can describe a PDE. Use ProblemBuilder; it is the one that trains anywhere:

import numpy as np
import pinneapple as pp
from pinneapple_physics import ProblemBuilder

spec = (ProblemBuilder("my_heat")
        .domain(x=(0.0, 1.0), t=(0.0, 1.0))
        .fields("u")
        .pde("heat_equation", alpha=0.01)
        .ic(field="u", fn=lambda X: np.sin(np.pi * X[:, 0:1]))
        .bc("dirichlet", field="u", value=0.0, on="x_boundary")
        .build())
sol = pp.solve(spec, method="pinn", epochs=2000)
print(sol.metadata())

SymbolicPDE (pinneapple_physics.symbolic_pde) compiles a SymPy residual with autograd through the expression tree. It is the advanced route: reach for it when the equation you need is not a kind the builder knows, and read compiler.py's module docstring first, which explains which of the two paths to use and why.

docs.title: What "it runs" means here
docs.text: pp.card(name) tries the cheapest method once and says whether the preset produced a field on this machine. Thirty-two of the forty presets whose boundaries are named geometry tags declare the box or cylinder those tags map onto, and pp.solve sends it for you, so they train from their name alone. When a preset still cannot run, the card names what is missing (FEniCS, OpenFOAM) and hands over standalone_snippet(name): the same equation and fields, on a box, with boundaries you set. pp.recommend(text) prefers a preset that runs and says which closer one it passed over.

docs.title: Adding an experiment / Como adicionar um experimento
docs.text: Every experiment in the repository is described by one manifest, experiment.json, next to its scripts or results. The Lab curation (A–F seal and next steps), the experiments site and the Flow Studio all read it through one loader, pinneapple_lab.manifest.load. You rarely write it by hand: the paths below write it for you.

docs.title: 1. A new example
docs.text:
python -m pinneapple_lab scaffold my_study          # examples/my_study: run.py, README.md, experiment.json
python examples/my_study/run.py                     # writes the manifest, registers it in the Lab, curates
python -m pinneapple_lab seal --explain manifest/examples/my_study    # its letter and what it lacks for the next

run.py is wrapped in pinneapple_lab.experiment(...):

from pinneapple_lab import experiment

with experiment("my_study", title="...", domain="structural mechanics", methods=["FEM"], params={"n": 64}) as ex:
    ...
    ex.log_metric("Kt", kt, unit="", how="max von Mises / nominal stress at the hole edge")
    ex.check("kt_vs_peterson", value=kt, reference=3.03, rtol=0.03, kind="reference", label="Kt vs Peterson")
    fig.savefig("examples/my_study/results/stress.png")      # recorded automatically
    ex.add_file("examples/my_study/results/wake.mp4")       # movies, viewers, data

On exit it records the parameters, the git commit, the environment and the wall time, writes experiment.json, imports it into the Lab as the item manifest/<id> (its checks are graded A–F with next steps, like any Lab run) and re-curates. An exception inside the block is recorded (the item is graded F) and re-raised. register=False writes the manifest only. The decorator form @experiment("name", ...) passes the capture to the function.

docs.title: 2. Other ways an experiment is captured
docs.text:
path what writes the manifest Lab experiments (pinneapple_lab.run, sweep) the runner writes experiment.json into every run folder; older run folders are read from run.json pinneapple_core.workflows runs WorkflowRunner.run writes runs/<id>/experiment.json (step outputs that are numbers become metrics) pp.solve(...) solution.to_experiment("out/folder", register=True) pp.compare(...) comparison.to_experiment("out/folder", register=True) (every metric of every method that ran) Flow Studio runs pinneapple_lab.manifest.from_flow_run(run, out_dir) (keys below) an existing folder python -m pinneapple_lab register examples/<folder> (generated from what the folder holds)

from_flow_run(run, out_dir) takes id, title, description, domain, nodes ([{"type": ...}], become the methods), modules, params, metrics ([{"name", "value", "unit", "how"}], measured values only; others are dropped), checks (as ctx.check records them), files and links, and writes out_dir/experiment.json.

docs.title: 3. The format (pinneapple.experiment/1)
docs.text:
schema, id, title, description, domain, methods, modules, params, scripts, metrics (name, value, unit, how), checks, files (figures, videos, viewers, data, paths relative to the manifest's folder), links (guide, script, pr), references, status (curated / not curated), lab (the Lab item it is linked to) and provenance (source, git, created, seconds, environment). See pinneapple_lab/manifest.py for an example.

Rules a manifest must meet (pinneapple_lab.manifest.validate): every metric has a finite measured value, a unit field ("" for dimensionless) and says how it was measured; every listed file exists; the schema is the current one. Nothing in a manifest is a placeholder: register fills only what the folder holds (title and description from the README or the first script's docstring, modules from the imports, figures and movies, the docs page that cites the folder, the pull requests whose merge changed it), leaves the rest empty, and marks methods found by name as inferred. Metrics come from a Lab run when the Lab has curated the folder's scripts, else the list is empty.

docs.title: Committed results
docs.text: A folder that commits measured results (results/*.json) is graded from them with pinneapple_lab.manifest.from_results(folder) and a rule set in pinneapple_lab.results_rules.RESULTS_RULES: Metric (a value, its unit and how it was measured), Flag (a verdict the study recorded, such as stall_margin_ok), CheckList (check records the study wrote, each with its own passed) and Bound (a value against the threshold the study's own test applies, cited as tests/test_x.py:LINE; a test checks the literal is on that line). Then python -m pinneapple_lab register <folder> grades it. A folder whose results a Lab repo_results source already reads is linked to that item instead (manifest.lab_items_for).

docs.title: 4. The CI gate
docs.text:
python scripts/check_experiment_manifests.py        # also: python -m pinneapple_lab manifests --check

It fails when an examples/* folder (other than names starting with _ or ., and scratch) has no experiment.json, when a manifest lists a file that does not exist or a metric without a value, and when a Lab run folder does not read as a valid manifest. CI runs it as a must-pass step.

docs.title: 5. Discovery
docs.text: pinneapple_lab.manifest.scan() finds every experiment.json under examples/ and every Lab run folder; a new folder with a manifest appears with no code change. python -m pinneapple_lab manifests lists them.

docs.title: 1. Um exemplo novo
docs.text:
python -m pinneapple_lab scaffold meu_estudo         # examples/meu_estudo: run.py, README.md, experiment.json
python examples/meu_estudo/run.py                    # grava o manifesto, registra no Lab e refaz a curadoria
python -m pinneapple_lab seal --explain manifest/examples/meu_estudo    # nível e o que falta para o seguinte

O run.py usa pinneapple_lab.experiment(...): ex.log_metric(nome, valor, unit=..., how=...) registra uma métrica medida (com unidade e como foi medida), ex.check(...) uma verificação (mesmos argumentos de ctx.check), e toda figura salva com savefig entra no manifesto; vídeos, visualizadores 3-D e dados entram com ex.add_file. Ao sair, grava parâmetros, commit git, ambiente e tempo, escreve experiment.json, importa-o no Lab como o item manifest/<id> (avaliado de A a F, com os próximos passos) e refaz a curadoria. Uma exceção dentro do bloco fica registrada (o item recebe F) e é propagada.

docs.title: 2. Outros caminhos
docs.text: Execuções do Lab (run, sweep) e de pinneapple_core.workflows gravam experiment.json na pasta da execução; pp.solve(...).to_experiment(pasta) e pp.compare(...).to_experiment(pasta) salvam o resultado; o Flow Studio chama pinneapple_lab.manifest.from_flow_run(run, pasta); uma pasta antiga entra com python -m pinneapple_lab register examples/<pasta>.

docs.title: 3. Regras
docs.text: Toda métrica tem valor medido, unidade ("" se adimensional) e diz como foi medida; todo arquivo listado existe. O register só preenche o que a pasta já tem e deixa o resto vazio; nenhum número é inventado.

docs.title: 4. Verificação no CI
docs.text: python scripts/check_experiment_manifests.py falha quando uma pasta examples/* não tem experiment.json válido, quando um manifesto aponta para um arquivo inexistente ou uma métrica sem valor, ou quando uma execução do Lab não é um manifesto válido. O CI roda essa verificação como etapa obrigatória.

docs.title: Agent Workbench: coding and engineering agents on a local model
docs.text:
pinneapple_llm.workbench is a team of agents that works in your projects the way a hosted coding assistant does, but with a model running on your own machine. A lead agent talks to you, reads the code, keeps a plan, makes changes, runs the tests and hands parts of the work to specialists. Every conversation is stored in a database so you can rate it and fine-tune the model on your own work.

It runs as a web app (or inside VS Code) started by one command. Nothing leaves your machine except internet searches, when you allow them.

The screenshots on this page come from the browser test, driven by a scripted model rather than a real one.

docs.title: What the agents can do
docs.text:
Tool What it does Approval (default auto policy) list_dir, read_file, glob, search browse and search the project never write_file, edit_file create files; replace an exact piece of text ask policy only run shell commands in the project: tests, linters, git, scripts read-only and test commands run; anything else asks run(background=true), job_output, job_stop servers, trainings, long simulations as run web_search, fetch_url search the internet, read pages and raw files never (can be turned off per session) github GitHub REST API: pull requests, issues, CI (needs GITHUB_TOKEN) writes ask show_file put a figure, screenshot, HTML report, PDF or video in the chat never reason_chain, reason_library, reason_check the chain of whys of a design with pinneapple_reason (report and timeline written in the project), its library of failure modes, one computed check (guide); the physics agent has them reason_chain asks under ask todo the plan shown beside the chat never delegate hand a self-contained task to a specialist never ask_user a question to you, with choices it waits for you start_session, send_to_session, list_sessions, session_status parallel sessions working on independent parts never schedule a message back into the session later (check a CI run or a long job) never

The paths are confined to the session's folder (symlinks included). Commands with ;, |, &&, $( ), rm, sudo, curl and similar always ask under auto. yolo asks for nothing: use it only in a throw-away folder.

The agents are Markdown files in pinneapple_llm/workbench/prompts/:

Agent Role lead understands the request, plans, edits, runs checks, delegates, has the change reviewed, reports explorer finds where things live and explains how they work (read-only) researcher internet and documentation search, other repositories, with sources coder implements a change and checks it tester writes and runs tests, reproduces failures reviewer critical review of the diff: bugs, weak tests, unmeasured numbers, misplaced logic physics PINNeAPPle problems, solvers and validation (pp.solve, pp.compare, pp.trust_card) reporter status reports with "with me" / "with you" checklists

All of them follow _common.md: look before changing, minimal changes in the local style, run the checks, never report an unmeasured number, never weaken a test. Edit any of them in the app (Agents). Your version is saved in ~/.pinneapple/workbench/agents/. A project can also carry its own in <project>/.pinneapple/agents/, and a new file adds a new agent the lead can delegate to.

docs.title: Install and start (Mac with Apple Silicon)
docs.text:
brew install ollama            # or the app from https://ollama.com; it uses the Mac's GPU (Metal)
ollama serve &                 # the Ollama app does this for you
pip install "pinneapple[workbench]"

python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench doctor       # memory, Ollama, model, Python packages: what to fix
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench pull         # downloads the model recommended for your memory
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench serve --workspace ~/code/my-project --language Português

The browser opens on http://127.0.0.1:8770. New session picks the folder, the model and the approval policy. pinneapple-workbench is the same command.

On Linux with an NVIDIA GPU the steps are the same; Ollama uses CUDA.

docs.title: Which model
docs.text:
doctor picks from the machine's memory (pinneapple_llm.workbench.models.RECOMMENDATIONS):

Memory Default model Size Notes 96 GB or more gpt-oss:120b ~65 GB MoE with 5B active parameters: fast for its size 32–64 GB qwen3-coder:30b ~19 GB MoE coding model with native tool calls; 3B active, fast on Apple Silicon 24 GB gpt-oss:20b ~14 GB good tool use for its size 16 GB qwen3:8b ~5 GB shorter, simpler tasks less qwen3:4b ~3 GB single-file edits and questions

Any other model works with --model. Models without native tool calls fall back to JSON tool calls in the text automatically. Other servers work through their OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

# LM Studio, llama.cpp llama-server, vLLM, or mlx_lm.server (often the fastest on a Mac)
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 --model <name>

Quality

No model that fits on a laptop matches the largest hosted models on long, multi-file work. Expect the local team to do well on focused tasks (a bug, a function with its test, a question about the code, a script) and to need more steering on large refactors. Measure the model you choose on your machine: eval (below) runs the same tasks for any model and reports pass/fail, time and tokens.

docs.title: Measure a model
docs.text:
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench eval --model qwen3-coder:30b --json eval-qwen.json
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench eval --model gpt-oss:20b

Each task builds a small project in a temporary folder and checks the outcome mechanically:

Task Pass condition fix_failing_test the suite passes, and the test is unchanged add_feature_with_test the new function is correct on hidden inputs, and has a test locate_code the answer names the right file and function

docs.title: In the terminal
docs.text:
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench run "the heat solver test fails since the last commit; find out why and fix it" \
    --workspace ~/code/my-project

Approvals and questions are asked in the terminal. The session is saved like the ones in the app.

docs.title: Inside VS Code
docs.text:
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench vscode      # copies the extension into ~/.vscode/extensions

Restart VS Code. Then:

  • PINNeAPPle: Open Agent Workbench (Cmd+Shift+P) opens the app beside your editor and starts the server for the open folder if it is not running.
  • Ask the agents about the selection (right click on selected code) starts a session with that code, its file and lines.

The interpreter, port and extra serve arguments are in the settings, under PINNeAPPle Agent Workbench.

docs.title: Internet search
docs.text: web_search uses, in order: your SearXNG instance (PINNEAPPLE_SEARXNG_URL, private, no key), the Brave Search API (BRAVE_API_KEY), the Tavily API (TAVILY_API_KEY), or DuckDuckGo's HTML endpoint (no key). fetch_url reads a page as text and GitHub blob links as raw files. The researcher agent clones repositories it needs to study into .research/ inside the workspace.

docs.title: The database
docs.text:
By default everything goes to ~/.pinneapple/workbench/sessions.sqlite. To use a PostgreSQL server you already run:

pip install "psycopg[binary]"
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench serve --db postgresql://user:password@host:5432/workbench
# or: export PINNEAPPLE_WORKBENCH_DB=postgresql://...
Table Content sessions folder, settings, the lead's message history events everything shown in the chat, in order (replayed when you reopen a session) model_calls every request to the model: input messages, tool specs, reply, agent, time, tokens feedback your 👍 / 👎 on a turn, with an optional note

docs.title: Fine-tune the model on your sessions
docs.text:
Rate turns with 👍 / 👎 as you work. Training data in the app shows what was recorded and exports the dataset:

From the terminal:

# 1. dataset: one example per agent run (the full trajectory with tool calls), 👎 turns left out,
#    secrets (tokens, keys, passwords) masked. --min-rating 1 keeps only 👍 turns.
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench finetune export --data ~/wb-data

# 2. LoRA training on the Mac (pip install mlx-lm), on the same model family you use in Ollama
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench finetune train --data ~/wb-data \
    --base mlx-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit --iters 600

# 3. serve base + adapter, and point the workbench at it
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench finetune serve --base mlx-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 \
    --model mlx-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit

# 4. compare with the base model on the same tasks
python -m pinneapple_llm.workbench eval --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 --model <same>

On NVIDIA, --engine peft trains with TRL + PEFT instead (pip install "pinneapple[finetune]" trl). --dry-run prints the training command without running it. Check the exact MLX repository name on huggingface.co/mlx-community before a long download.

A few hundred good trajectories of your own kind of work help most with your conventions, tools and project structure. They do not add general capability the base model lacks.

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
from pinneapple_llm.workbench import ApprovalPolicy, Session, Store, make_backend

store = Store()                                   # or Store("postgresql://...")
sid = store.create("/path/to/project", {"policy": "auto"})
session = Session(make_backend("ollama", "qwen3-coder:30b"), "/path/to/project",
                  policy=ApprovalPolicy("auto"),
                  on_event=lambda e: store.add_event(sid, e),
                  on_model_call=lambda c: store.add_model_call(sid, c))
print(session.send("Where is the boundary condition applied in the heat solver?"))

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• The server listens on 127.0.0.1. If you bind it elsewhere, set --token, and keep in mind the agents run commands as your user.
  • Prefer auto or ask in real projects, and commit before large changes so git diff shows what the agents did.
  • Files shown in the chat are served only from the session's folder.

docs.title: An end-to-end CFD surrogate study: the Ahmed body
docs.text: From geometry to a digital twin and back to wind-tunnel data, every step a library call and every number measured: examples/end_to_end/ahmed_body (scripts 01-07), the app apps/ahmed_twin and the flow pinneapple_flow/flows/ahmed_body_end_to_end.json run the same calls.

docs.title: Why the Ahmed body
docs.text: It is the standard bluff-body test case of road-vehicle aerodynamics: a public, fully specified geometry (1.044 x 0.389 x 0.288 m, 0.1 m front radii, a 0.222 m rear slant), a published drag curve against the slant angle (Ahmed, Ramm & Faltin, SAE 840300, 1984, 60 m/s) that has a known difficulty (the drag peak just below 30 degrees, which steady RANS does not reproduce), and an external flow that the generic OpenFOAM pipeline (pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.external_flow.ExternalFlow) already runs for any STL. A finned heat sink would have given correlations rather than measurements for the inverse step; the Ahmed body gives measurements.

docs.title: Stages and the calls behind them
docs.text: Stage Library Example Geometry: parametric (make_body, a fixed 1751-point field template for every variant) and real CAD (ahmed_cad: OpenCASCADE B-rep through gmsh, STEP + STL) imported back with checks and named patches (import_body) pinneapple_autolab.domains.ahmed 01_cfd_campaign.py cad Simulator: snappyHexMesh with 5 prism layers, simpleFoam k-omega SST with wall functions, moving road, half model; per run checkMesh, mesh quality, residuals, force stationarity, mass balance from phi (pinneapple_check), y+ range (qa_checks, run_trust_report) AhmedAero Mesh family with a constant refinement ratio sqrt(2); Richardson extrapolation and GCI (Celik et al. 2008) pinneapple_autolab.study.mesh_study 01 ... mesh, 02_analysis.py Validation against the wind tunnel ahmed_study.grid_and_validation 01 ... validation, 02 DOE: maximin Latin hypercube with discrepancy and minimum distance against random designs; resumable runs with a cost ledger pinneapple_autolab.study.campaign 01 ... doe Dataset: scalars, surface Cp, provenance as a DatasetSpec; slant > 34 deg held out as the extrapolation split pinneapple_autolab.study.dataset, ahmed_study.study_dataset 02 Surrogates at equal data and budget (GP, MLP ensemble, response surface; POD-GP, POD-MLP, POD-RBF, DeepONet), 5-fold CV, cross-conformal 90 % intervals, physics checks on predictions, a written selection rule pinneapple_autolab.study.benchmark 02 Sobol indices, NSGA-II with an uncertainty constraint and CFD checks of the Pareto picks, acquisition by uncertainty against random runs pinneapple_autolab.study.extras 02, 03_more_cfd.py Inverse: amortised posterior (mixture density network) of the slant from a drag measurement; synthetic checks first; least squares and Metropolis baselines pinneapple_analysis.inverse_problems.amortized, ahmed_study.inverse 04_inverse.py Digital twin: sliders, Cp in 3-D, 90 % band, trust-region warning, verifying CFD pinneapple_autolab.study.twin, apps/ahmed_twin 05_twin.py Visuals: Blender Cycles stills on a dark product stage, a short narrated film in English (title card, CFD orbit, slices, surrogate sweep, end card with the measured numbers), three.js viewer, OpenUSD stage with the trust decision ahmed_study.visuals, pp.viz.render(..., background="dark", cmap="rdbu", floor=True), pinneapple_tools.visualization.studio.captions (caption, title_card, narrate, mux_audio) 06_visuals.py Evidence report (HTML), hashed evidence package, cost accounting, summary.json (every measured number with its unit and how it was measured), experiment manifest ahmed_study.study_report, study_costs on pinneapple_autolab.study.report; Flow node study.report 07_report.py

docs.title: The physics checks on surrogate predictions
docs.text: A surrogate's prediction is checked like a solver result (ahmed.prediction_checks), on a Sobol sample of the design space: drag and pressure drag positive; friction drag positive and falling as the speed (the Reynolds number) rises; the pressure coefficient never above the incompressible stagnation value 1 (with a margin) and close to 1 on the nose; and the pressure drag integrated from the predicted Cp field equal to the scalar model's pressure drag, within the tolerance the CFD itself shows on the same template. A family that fails one is not eligible.

docs.title: The field-scalar consistency check: the decision
docs.text:
The Cp surrogate's eligibility hinged on one check, and its first formulation was wrong in two ways. It integrated the predicted Cp over the template, compared the result with the selected CD_pressure model at 48 Sobol points, and required the maximum difference to be within the CFD's own template gap at its 95th percentile plus 0.01. A maximum against a percentile fails even the CFD's own Cp fields (their largest template gap on the 54 campaign cases, 0.069, is above that 0.052), and the scalar model's error (test RMSE 0.010, mean calibrated half width 0.045) was counted against the field. No family was eligible under it.

The check now (ahmed.prediction_checks) holds the surrogate to the same quantile as the data it is compared with: over 128 Sobol points, |integrated Cp - predicted CD_pressure| is divided by the quadrature sum of the CFD's template gap at its 95th percentile (measured on every CFD case by ahmed_study.template_integral, no added margin) and the scalar model's calibrated 90 % half width at that point (two independent bounds), and the 95th percentile of that ratio must be <= 1. Subtracting the half width instead of adding it in quadrature was tried and rejected: a 90 % bound is not a typical error, and that variant let a field whose raw gap is twice the CFD's pass. Each check reports the raw p95 and maximum of the difference as well, and the report states both outcomes.

docs.title: Reference data and what was verified
docs.text: ahmed.MEASUREMENTS holds every wind-tunnel set the study uses, with its source and a note per value on how far it was verified from the build environment (the SAE papers and the ERCOFTAC database are not reachable from it; secondary sources found by web search confirmed the 12.5 and 35 deg values and the Reynolds number of Ahmed et al. 1984, and the 25 deg value as widely quoted; 0, 30 and 40 deg remain the repository's transcription). Lienhart & Becker (2003; LSTM Erlangen, 40 m/s, 25 and 35 deg) is in the table with its conditions only: its drag values could not be obtained, so the inverse stage reports that set as not measured here rather than inverting a number it cannot source.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: The measured tables (grid convergence, validation, surrogate errors and coverage, inverse results, costs) are in examples/end_to_end/ahmed_body/README.md and results/report.html, written from the JSON files in results/.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Steady RANS with k-omega SST and wall functions; the stilts of the wind-tunnel model are left out; the reference is the total drag of one wind-tunnel campaign. The surrogates are valid in the DOE's box (slant 0-40 deg, clearance 30-80 mm, speed 20-60 m/s) and the twin says when a slider point is far from every CFD run.

docs.title: Antenna design: an end-fire Vivaldi with an external FEM solver
docs.text:
This guide runs, end to end, a study of an antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) for 2–4 GHz with a 10 dBi target, the kind of study usually done by hand in a FEM simulator: a few variants, a table of S11 and gains, a plot. Here the FEM solver is EMerge (open source, pip install emerge), the antenna is an open parametric model written for this library, and PINNeAPPle adds the physical limits, the checks, the surrogate errors measured honestly, the design loop and a trust card per prediction.

Everything lives in pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.antenna; the example examples/use_cases/antennas/vivaldi_2to4ghz.py only calls it.

The same audit written as a datasheet -- the external solver's table read back, checked against the end-fire bound, and rendered to PDF without a new solve -- is the pattern in Design reports.

pip install emerge                                                         # GPL-2.0, called, never copied
python examples/use_cases/antennas/vivaldi_2to4ghz.py --quick              # 3 designs x 2 frequencies, ~3 min
python examples/use_cases/antennas/vivaldi_2to4ghz.py                      # 16 designs x 5 frequencies + fine runs
python examples/use_cases/antennas/vivaldi_2to4ghz.py --package <dir>      # an external study package

docs.title: 1. How long must the antenna be? (bounds)
docs.text:
A Vivaldi radiates end-fire, along the board. Its gain is bounded by its length L, not by its broadside area: an end-fire travelling-wave antenna is at best a Hansen–Woodyard line source, D ≈ 7.28 L/λ (ordinary end-fire: D ≈ 4 L/λ; C. A. Balanis, Antenna Theory, ch. 6). The aperture formula G = η 4πA/λ² applies to a broadside aperture; used on a 100 × 200 mm Vivaldi it gives an optimistic bound for the wrong direction.

from pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.antenna import bounds

bounds.min_length(10.0, 2e9)               # 0.2059 m: 10 dBi at 2 GHz needs L >= 206 mm (HW limit)
bounds.min_length(10.0, 2e9, "ordinary")   # 0.3747 m
bounds.feasibility_frequency(10.0, 0.206)  # 2.00e9 Hz: below it no 206 mm design reaches 10 dBi
f [GHz] L for 10 dBi, Hansen–Woodyard [mm] ordinary end-fire [mm] 2.0 206 375 2.5 165 300 3.0 137 250 3.5 118 214 4.0 103 187

The feasibility frontier (lowest frequency where the target fits a board of length L): 2.75 GHz for 150 mm, 2.00 GHz for 206 mm, 1.58 GHz for 260 mm. A 10 dBi requirement down to 2 GHz on a board shorter than 206 mm is infeasible whatever the flare, the slots or the director; no simulation is needed to know it.

docs.title: 2. The open AVA model (ava)
docs.text:
AVAParams + layout describe the antenna in millimetres; layout is pure NumPy and raises InvalidGeometry for designs that cannot be built (arms thinner than 0.5 mm, slots cutting through an arm, a director touching the flare), which the DOE skips. simulate builds it in EMerge:

  • substrate εr 3.55, tan δ 0.003, h 1.524 mm; PEC conductors of zero thickness;
  • top layer: 50 Ω microstrip (width from Pozar eq. 3.197: 3.41 mm) then an exponential flare towards +x; bottom layer: ground of width Wg and length Lo, a linear taper to the strip width (the transition / balun), then the mirrored flare; optional corrugation slots (nslot, Ls, ws, ps) on the outer edges and an elliptical director (dir_a, dir_b, dir_x);
  • air box with air · λ of margin and a second-order absorbing boundary, lumped 50 Ω port at the board edge;
  • mesh size res · λ at the simulated frequency (one mesh per frequency);
  • per frequency: complex S11, directivity, IEEE gain and realized gain at boresight (+y) and at the peak, radiation efficiency, the far field (θ, φ, E_θ, E_φ) in ff_<f>GHz.npz, and the radiated power two ways (integral of the pattern, Poynting flux through the box) for the power-closure check.

docs.title: 3. Running a parametric CLI solver (runner)
docs.text:
CLISimulator(argv, workdir) runs any script that takes --params JSON --freq GHz --out DIR (flags configurable) and writes result.json: one process per design and per frequency, a timeout, the exit status and the peak memory of each child (os.wait4). Lessons measured on this 4-core, 15 GB container and built in:

  • EMerge's PARDISO backend can die with SIGBUS without a usable MKL: the AVA CLI uses SuperLU (emerge._emerge.solver._PARDISO_AVAILABLE = False); fallback_args re-runs a sample once after a SIGBUS;
  • three frequencies in one process with SuperLU went past 15 GB and were SIGKILLed: one frequency per process (also gives each frequency its own λ-sized mesh);
  • grid.model_S fails with a single frequency: the CLI reads grid.S;
  • the first EMerge run compiles Numba kernels (about 4 min here, 375 s for the first 3 GHz solve); later runs load them from the cache.

read_table / write_table handle the (design, frequency) table: tag, the parameters, f_GHz, S11_dB, D_bore_dBi, G_bore_dBi, Greal_bore_dBi, D_peak_dBi, Greal_peak_dBi, rad_eff (CSV, TSV or whitespace).

docs.title: 4. Checks of every row (checks)
docs.text:
antenna_checks(row) returns a TrustReport (supports / contradicts / not_run):

check relation critical realized_gain G_realized = G + 10 log10(1-|S11|²) no efficiency_is_G_over_D e = G/D no efficiency_le_1 e <= 1 (+1 %) yes peak_ge_boresight peak >= boresight no directivity_le_hw D <= 7.28 L/λ + 0.5 dB no s11_resolved a vector-fitted (interpolated) S11 needs >= 5 solved frequencies no power_closure pattern power = Poynting flux through the box, within 10 % no

Missing inputs make a check not_run, never a silent pass.

docs.title: 5. Surrogates and honest errors (surrogates)
docs.text: Four models, all predicting a column from (design, frequency): the per-frequency mean (baseline), the HW limit plus one fitted offset, ridge regression on physical features (log L/λ, W/λ, Wa/λ, slots on/off, director on/off), and a Gaussian process on the same features with the HW limit as prior mean (its std is the stated uncertainty). lodo(table, target) leaves one design out at a time — all its frequencies together — because leaving one row out lets the model see the same design at the neighbouring frequencies. holdout uses a fixed test set. coverage95 says how often the truth fell inside ±1.96 std.

docs.title: 6. Design loop (design, study)
docs.text:
• doe(n): LHS or Sobol over AVA_RANGES (configurable), unbuildable designs skipped and counted;
  • optimize(models, freqs): NSGA-II (pinneapple_design.design_optimizer) maximising the minimum realized gain over the band and minimising Lb·W, with max S11 <= -10 dB over the band, inside the span of the trained designs;
  • active_learning(simulate, table, freqs): GP variance picks the next designs (pinneapple_data.active_learning.VarianceBasedAL), EMerge verifies them, and the error of the prediction made before the simulation is recorded;
  • multi_fidelity(coarse, fine, target): many coarse runs (res 0.25 λ), a few fine ones (0.2 λ); the coarse-to-fine bias per frequency, validated leaving one fine design out;
  • prediction_card(model, params, f, train): in the training domain (feature space, critical), buildable (critical), std below 1 dB, below the HW limit, LODO error known and below 1.5 dB.

study.open_study(out) chains all of it; study.package_study(dir, out) reproduces an external package.

docs.title: 7. Measured results (open model, this container)
docs.text:
All numbers below were measured by vivaldi_2to4ghz.py (full mode) on a 4-core, 15 GB container, EMerge 2.8.9, SuperLU, files in examples/use_cases/antennas/results/ (summary.json, results_*.csv, figures). Coarse mesh res = 0.25 λ (3 160 to 9 721 tetrahedra), air margin 0.25 λ, fine mesh res = 0.2 λ.

Cost. 125 EMerge processes (one frequency each), all ok: median 10.8 s, peak memory 2.85 GB per process, 1 595 s of solver time, 1 633 s for the whole study (DOE, fine runs, checks, LODO, NSGA-II, verification, active learning). --quick (12 processes): 184 s. The very first EMerge run on a machine adds about 4 min of Numba compilation. The first 3 GHz solve, repeated later through the runner, gave the same S11 to the last digit (−19.431 dB).

DOE. 16 buildable designs out of 31 LHS samples (15 rejected by layout before any solve).

Against the target. No simulated design (20 designs × 5 frequencies, plus the optimiser's pick) reaches 10 dBi realized gain anywhere in the band. Best realized boresight gain per frequency: 5.4 dBi at 2 GHz, 7.1 at 2.5, 7.9 at 3.0, 9.5 at 3.5, 9.1 dBi at 4 GHz. The peak directivity stays 1.6 dB (best case) and 4.3 dB (median) below the Hansen–Woodyard limit of each design's length, so directivity_le_hw never failed; at 2 GHz even the limit of the longest board (260 mm) is 11.0 dBi. Only 3 of the 20 designs keep S11 ≤ −10 dB over the whole band.
